findings.summary: The PENDING+recovery resume path commits the completed post-state with a bare `chore(...) recover ...` message (no idempotency receipt trailers) and then mark_aborted, discarding the claim. A same-key retry reclaims the record from ABORTED and re-executes write_fn, so recovery is not idempotent and can double-commit / repeat side effects, violating spec 3.2(a) `复用原 claim，不得重复提交、不得重复副作用（重复恢复 = 返回原 receipt）`.

A crash between ledger.prepare() and git_commit leaves a PREPARED record whose files are fully written (post-state) but whose commit was never published. _reconcile_pending only resumes `record.state == "PENDING"` records, so this judgeable resume case (HEAD == base_sha, content == post-state) falls through to mark_broken (fail-closed) instead of continuing commit+finalize, leaving a recoverable scene permanently BROKEN rather than committed-with-receipt or reverted-clean (spec 2 and 3.2(a)).

The spec 4.1 freeze acceptance test (#1) requiring crash injection after write_fn success but before git_commit -> recovery to {committed+clean, reverted-clean} with idempotent repeat is absent from the suite. No test exercises the `_reconcile_pending` resume/rollback branches (`"action": "resume"`/`"rollback"` never appear in tests); the only reconcile recovery test injects a post-commit finalize failure. Test-pass determination relies solely on the seal-verified implement.json record (1403/1403), which does not establish coverage of the spec's central crash window.

Recovery receipts written through mark_aborted/mark_broken omit most of the spec 5 minimal schema: resume records only action+commit_sha, rollback only action+paths, fail-closed only action+detail, and the discard branch stores a bare string with no action or a/b/c/d classification. actor, timestamp, base_sha, terminal state, and classification are missing, weakening recovery auditability.
